active_family: 294 continuous scaffold fixed-horizon joint conditional-law model
current_bottleneck: The continuous scaffold family is live, but the current low-frequency basis is too globally smooth. It improved level-law fit and removed the old over-reversion failure, but it cannot express enough localized curvature or mid-window reversion to preserve MR, worst-cell cointegration robustness, and jump timing.
last_result_summary: Iteration 151 compared 293h against 294a and concluded that 294a is a genuine new mechanism class, not another support-branch tradeoff. The failure pattern flipped from over-reversion to under-reversion, which isolates the new bottleneck to the scaffold basis itself rather than support representation or support-use geometry.
next_step_recommendation: Ideate 294b as a sharper continuous scaffold follow-up: keep the 294 family, but replace the overly smooth global basis with a more localized continuous scaffold object and avoid any return to support codebooks.

current_best_note: 282b is still the cleanest current Stage B objective frontier at 5/11, but 284b and 285a strengthen the conclusion that the real cap is now the Stage A support object rather than the Stage B weighting law.
